title: THE SHORT CHAIN · 20 MINUTES, OR NOTHING AT ALL
vibe: yellow · compressed · 20 minutes · a practice, not a beating — and skipping it is a real option, not a failure
why: Six hours of sleep and light soreness after four hundred and twenty-six reps of pull and press. That is a yellow day by the numbers, and you already said you are short on time and may not train at all. So this is deliberately built to be small. Twenty minutes, one bell, one chain, no clock pressure, and it is written so that stopping after two rounds is a completed workout rather than a partial one. If the window never opens, take the rest day. You trained hard four days running through jet lag and the last one was triple the written volume, so a day off is banked value, not lost ground. If the window does open, here is what fits it. Your shoulders, lats and chest took everything yesterday, so today touches them as little as possible. Your legs have now had two full days out of the lead role and the jet lag has had a day to fade, so the load goes back to the hips and the legs where there is something available. And the shape changes again: this is a flow, one continuous chain where the bell never touches the floor until the round is done. No stations, no descending list, no rest intervals. You count rounds and you judge them by whether they looked good, not by how wrecked you feel. That is the point of a flow on a yellow day: it is the one shape that produces real work while giving you a quality standard instead of an intensity standard to chase.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · DAY C · THE FLOW
blocks.meta: ~4 min · Moves Method Day C · one continuous moving sequence, no reps to count

items.name: ROCK-BACKS · 45 sec
items.detail: On hands and knees, rock the hips back toward the heels and forward again, easy and rhythmic. Let the low back and hips unlock. Do not count, just move for forty-five seconds.

items.name: CROSS-CRAWL AND ROLLING · 60 sec
items.detail: Standing cross-crawls, opposite elbow to opposite knee, thirty seconds. Then lie down and roll from your back to your stomach and back again, led by one arm, then the other. Contralateral wiring, and it costs nothing.

items.name: DEEP SQUAT SIT · 60 sec
items.detail: Sit into the bottom of a squat and stay there, elbows inside the knees, and gently rock side to side and forward and back. A full minute. Today the legs are the main event, so this is the one that matters.

items.name: PRIMER · 10 SWINGS + 5 GOBLET SQUATS · 16 kg
items.detail: One easy pass, light bell, just to find the hinge and the squat before the chain starts.

blocks.text: Day C off the Moves Method menu — the flow day, matched to a flow session. Day A ran 08-20, Day B ran 08-19, Day C last ran 08-18. Four minutes, because the whole session is twenty.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE CHAIN · 3 ROUNDS PER SIDE
blocks.meta: ~10 min · ONE 16 kg or 20 kg bell · 3 ROUNDS PER SIDE (6 total passes) · floor 2 rounds per side, stretch 4
blocks.format: single-bell flow — one continuous chain, five movements, the bell does NOT touch the floor until the round is finished. Then switch hands.
blocks.workRest: One round is the five movements below, straight through, same hand. Set the bell down, shake out, take 45 to 60 seconds, then run it on the other hand. That pair is one round per side. THREE ROUNDS PER SIDE is the target. Two is a completed session on a yellow day.

items.name: 1 · SWING x 8
items.detail: One-arm swing to chest height. Snap the hips, let the arm be a rope. This sets the rhythm for everything that follows.

items.name: 2 · CLEAN x 5
items.detail: From the last swing, tame the arc and land the bell quietly in the rack. Five. If it bangs your forearm, you are muscling it up instead of guiding it in.

items.name: 3 · FRONT SQUAT x 5
items.detail: Bell stays racked. Sit down between your hips, elbow tight to the ribs, chest tall. Five. This is the reason the day exists — your legs are the only fresh thing you own right now.

items.name: 4 · REVERSE LUNGE x 5
items.detail: Still racked, same side. Step back, knee to just off the floor, drive through the front heel. Five on the same leg. Loaded on one side makes this a midline exercise as much as a leg one, which is how the core block gets paid today.

items.name: 5 · HALO x 5, then set it down
items.detail: Bell by the horns, circle it around your head, five times, slow. This is the release valve — it opens the shoulder you hammered yesterday instead of loading it. Then the bell touches the floor for the first time in the round.

items.name: THE STANDARD · QUALITY, NOT SURVIVAL
items.detail: This is a yellow day and a flow, so the rule is simple: every round should look like the one before it. The moment a clean gets sloppy or a squat gets short, that round was the last good one and you are done. Stopping at four passes because they were clean beats grinding out six ugly ones. Use the 16 if the 20 makes the lunges wobble.

blocks.text: Seeded off Neupert's Half Olympic Light, the clean-front-squat chain, opened out into a continuous single-bell flow with the press swapped for a halo so your shoulders get mobility instead of more volume. The flow shape has not run since 07-27.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · EASY RUN · 6 MIN
blocks.meta: 6 min · flat at 1 percent · 12.2 to 12.9 km/h · your own easy band, nothing clever
blocks.format: continuous, one speed, no surges and no grade

items.name: 6 MIN CONTINUOUS · 12.2 to 12.9 km/h
items.detail: Your easy band, roughly 7:30 to 7:55 a mile. Pick where in the band it feels right in the first minute and then leave the dial alone. No grade because yesterday and Wednesday both had one, no surges because it is a yellow day, and no distance target because six minutes is the whole point. If the twenty minutes has to become twelve, this is the block to cut.

blocks.text: Short and flat. The run is the constant, so it stays in even on a compressed day, but today it is the smallest version of itself rather than the place the work happens.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.text: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch, 45 seconds a side, back glute squeezed. Then a doorway pec stretch, 30 seconds a side, because yesterday is still in there. Then a minute of slow nasal breathing, longer out than in. Done.

timer.emomUnit: No clock on this one. Block 1 is 3 ROUNDS PER SIDE counted by hand, judged on quality — not a timed block. Use the countdown only for the 6-minute run.
